source.title: Bayesian Deep Convolutional Networks with Many Channels are Gaussian Processes
source.authors: Roman Novak; Lechao Xiao; Jaehoon Lee; Yasaman Bahri; Greg Yang; Jiri Hron; Daniel A. Abolafia; Jeffrey Pennington; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares test performance across CNN, locally connected, and fully connected architectures and studies width scaling, using its own CIFAR-10 experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports architecture and width results relevant to V2 and V3. Its references to Zhang et al. and Neyshabur et al. are prior-work citations, not this study's results. It does not test random-label memorization, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: Own CIFAR-10 experiments compare finite CNNs, LCNs and FCNs for V3 and measure held-out performance as already-interpolating CNNs and LCNs widen for V2. This study is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive the infinite-width Bayesian CNN–GP correspondence, report competitive CNN-GP performance, and find that carefully tuned finite CNNs achieve better performance without pooling. They conjecture an equivariance contribution while leaving the separate roles of optimization and finite width unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares CNNs, LCNs, FCNs, and their infinite-width GP counterparts rather than reproducing the specified studies' training setups. Networks use Adam in the general setup, with additional CIFAR-10 experiments using SGD; datasets, architectures, and selection procedures differ.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture, pooling, width, nonlinearity, learning rate, weight decay, batch size, and training-accuracy filtering are varied across experiments; the authors report that these choices affect performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Without pooling, infinite-width Bayesian CNNs and LCNs have identical GP predictions; carefully tuned finite CNNs can outperform their corresponding GPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefits of weight sharing depend on inference method and pooling; finite gradient-trained CNNs can outperform infinite-width Bayesian counterparts.

record.problems: The central Figure 1 architecture comparison is presented graphically; its plotted values are not extracted as exact numbers. Some large configurations were not evaluated due to time and memory limits. The paper says CNN-GP with pooling was not broadly compared with CNNs because of computational limits.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted from figure-only width sweeps in Figures 6 and 9; those plots support the width discussion but do not provide recoverable row values here. Cited prior-work results were excluded.

untested.parts: Fixed-random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.

The specified one-hidden-layer ReLU setting and a width sweep without explicit regularization. Here learning rate, weight decay and sometimes batch size are selected separately at each width; the interpolation-threshold peak is not established.
Learning sparse local connections within FCNs, initialization from trained CNNs, and finite gradient-trained architecture comparisons on MNIST, CIFAR-100 and SVHN.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD under controlled tuning budgets.
Held-out batch-size penalties under matched epoch budgets and their recovery through recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus random examples.

missing.what: Figure 1's finite FCN–LCN–CNN comparison, including pooling conditions, is needed to assess the local-connectivity component of V3. Record the architecture-specific accuracies and widths; do not combine finite networks with their GP counterparts.
The finite CNN-with-pooling result is omitted: 14.85% test error with perfect training accuracy and 15.65% in the unrestricted selection condition, versus FCN's 45.52% and 44.73%.

record.verdict_notes: Width-sweep results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as undeclared missing results. They support a new architectural setting for V2, without establishing its no-explicit-regularization condition. The paper inconsistently names the finite-network optimizer: figures and discussion say SGD, while the experimental setup specifies Adam.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
The width experiments use multi-layer CNNs and LCNs, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10. Width-sweep values are figure-only, so no result row was extracted.

The study does not test the cited LeCun et al. 1998 results, sparse local connections learned by fully connected networks, or initialization of a fully connected network from a trained convolutional network.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD, including the listed tuning and recovery conditions.
A comparison of large and small batches under fixed epoch budgets and the listed recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
